items.title: AI agents prefer specific disposable email services during identity attacks
items.summary: A joint investigation by Okta Threat Intelligence and Permiso's P0 Labs has identified that when asked to create accounts for security testing purposes, AI agents almost universally choose the services of one specific provider.

items.title: Former ShinyHunters-affiliated cluster O-UNC-053 moves to new INCEPTION leak site | Threat Intelligence
items.summary: In November 2026, organizations targeted by cluster O-UNC-053 appeared on a new data leak site branded as INCEPTION, rather than the previous ShinyHunters site.

items.title: Agentic attack tools accelerate reconnaissance of identity flows | Threat Intelligence
items.summary: Okta Threat Intelligence is investigating a large set of reconnaissance, fraudulent registration, and attempted intrusion activity across hundreds of tenants.

items.title: Credential stuffing attacks poised to accelerate with AI | Threat Intelligence
items.summary: Credential stuffing is poised to increase with AI, allowing attackers to reach greater scale. Here's how CIAM organizations can defend against it.

items.title: Multi-agent attack tools leave no stone unturned | Threat Intelligence
items.summary: Okta has observed an explosion in agents performing recon, making it essential to identify and remediate misconfigurations before agents find and exploit them.

items.title: When enrollment isn't enough: How attackers trick users into MFA downgrades | Threat Intelligence
items.summary: Attackers use MFA downgrades to trick users into using weaker authentication. Learn why enforcing phishing-resistant MFA is critical for protecting your organization.

items.title: Detecting shadow AI agents with advanced posture checks
items.summary: Okta has released a set of 24 detections for osquery, which is part of Okta Verify, to detect possible unauthorized AI tools running on devices.

items.title: Signing in without actually signing in | Threat Intelligence
items.summary: The cybercriminal market for hijacked AI accounts is flourishing as threat actors seek to lower their costs and obscure attribution for attacks.

items.title: First on the scene of the cybercrime
items.summary: Okta Threat Intelligence (OTI) recently hit a significant milestone: we sent our 10,000th suspicious domain notification to a customer.

items.title: Using advanced posture checks as a tooling watchdog
items.summary: Adversaries love to make life difficult for defenders. One of the best ways for attackers to operate undetected is to disable security tools on a compromised device.
